alerts.narrative: WIN-01 recorded 900 failed sign-ins for account admin from one source address.
The gateway saw one password tried against 70 employee accounts within five minutes.
Repeated guesses targeted the single Linux account backupsvc until authentication succeeded.
WIN-02 launched powershell.exe with an encoded command downloaded by the user.
LINUX-01 executed a curl pipeline through /bin/bash from a temporary directory.
The endpoint started cmd.exe /c whoami from an unsigned installer.
A spreadsheet attachment required the user to open invoice-review.xlsm and enabled malicious content.
The mail gateway delivered payroll-update.zip as a targeted attachment to Finance.
A public web server spawned a shell immediately after requests exploited an unpatched endpoint.
A valid dormant contractor account authenticated to the VPN from an unusual country.
The browser redirected the analyst to an exploit page that executed code without a download prompt.
An exposed remote administration service accepted an external session using a compromised account.
A newly inserted USB device copied and launched worm.exe on the Windows workstation.
A suspicious process opened LSASS and read its memory for credential material.
The infostealer read saved login data from the Chrome user profile database.
A service process invoked Windows Management Instrumentation to launch calc.exe remotely.
The host created a scheduled task named UpdateCheck that ran an unknown executable.
An unsigned binary called low-level Windows Native API functions to start a child process.
The user clicked a shortened link in a targeted message and the browser loaded a credential lure.
A fake software update prompted the user to copy and run a command in the terminal.
After 600 failed logons, WIN-03 accepted the password and launched encoded PowerShell.
Finance received quote.xlsm; opening the malicious attachment started cmd.exe /c payload.exe.
Requests exploited the public portal, then /bin/bash executed a downloaded script.
A stolen VPN account entered through the external service and ran a PowerShell discovery command.
The user opened benefits.docm, after which a process read LSASS memory.
Many authentication failures affected several accounts, but the source pattern was incomplete.
A script interpreter launched an obfuscated command; telemetry could not distinguish cmd from PowerShell.
A user interaction preceded execution of an unknown file delivered outside recorded mail telemetry.
An external login used correct credentials, but ownership of the account could not be confirmed.
The web process crashed after a crafted request and later spawned a child process; exploit success is uncertain.
The approved patch service installed the monthly Windows security update and rebooted normally.
A developer ran the signed company inventory script during the documented maintenance window.
The vulnerability scanner completed an authorized scan from the registered scanner address.
The backup agent authenticated with its managed service account and completed the scheduled backup.
An administrator opened PowerShell to run the approved health-check script under change ticket CHG-42.
